title: White Poplar: Ancient White Poplars You Can Visit
meta_description: Fast-spreading and rarely left to age. Three survive: Lithuania's largest known, a Warsaw natural monument, an Amsterdam veteran kept for its age alone.
intro: White poplars rarely get the chance to grow old. The species spreads fast by root suckers and gets cleared as a nuisance long before it reaches any real size, which is part of why the three mapped here stand out. Lithuania's Vainiai Poplar is the giant of the three, 6.85 metres round and among the largest of its kind recorded in the country, still standing in a former manor park that has otherwise reverted to scrub. Warsaw's example, in a small Rakowiec neighbourhood park, was made a natural monument in 1987 and shares its corner with two other protected trees. Amsterdam's is the odd one out: its own protection register admits it is no longer an impressive specimen and keeps it listed anyway, on the strength of being, most likely, the oldest living thing in its park. Three very different reasons to notice the same overlooked species.
